messages.summary:
## Objective
- Continue and finish the existing game in the repository as a complete, playable game.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Treated the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham Three.js project as the game to finish.
- Added Enter/Space keyboard support to advance dialogue, complementing the existing on-screen Continue button.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing game files and confirmed the project already contains a 3D city, story campaign, combat, collectibles, riddles, character swapping, vehicles, touch controls, and replay modes.
- Started a local HTTP server on port 3002 and opened the game in Playwright.
- Captured and inspected screenshots at `/tmp/opencode/gotham-check.jpg`, `/tmp/opencode/gotham-dialogue.jpg`, and `/tmp/opencode/gotham-play.jpg`.
- Modified `game.js` so Enter or Space advances dialogue while dialogue is active.

### Active
- Continue testing the game’s core gameplay flow and fix any issues that prevent completing the campaign.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest screenshot `/tmp/opencode/gotham-play.jpg` and current browser state.
2. Test movement, combat, collectibles/riddles, boss progression, and replay flow; patch any blockers.
3. Check `git diff` and summarize the completed game and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, story, controls, combat, UI logic; contains the uncommitted dialogue keyboard change.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and touch controls.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- The game is titled “BATMAN: SHADOWS OF GOTHAM”; the main campaign objective chain is gang operation → eight clues → Riddler → Two-Face.
- There is also a villain replay mode, but it does not appear to end when both heroes are defeated; they rally and continue fighting.
- `game.js` imports Three.js from `https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Browser output included a missing `/favicon.ico` 404 and WebGL performance warnings; no gameplay-breaking module error was observed.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Finish the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a complete, playable game.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and its campaign rather than starting a new project.
- Add Enter/Space keyboard support to advance dialogue, alongside the Continue button.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing game and confirmed it includes a 3D city, campaign, combat, collectibles, riddles, character swapping, vehicles, touch controls, and replay modes.
- Started a local server on port 3002 and opened the game in Playwright.
- Added Enter/Space dialogue advancement in `game.js`.

### Active
- Test the gameplay flow and fix any blockers to completing the campaign.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest screenshot `/tmp/opencode/gotham-play.jpg` and current browser state.
2. Test movement, combat, collectibles/riddles, boss progression, and replay flow; patch any blockers.
3. Review `git diff` and summarize the completed game and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, story, controls, combat, UI logic, and the uncommitted dialogue keyboard change.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and touch controls.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Campaign objective chain: gang operation → eight clues → Riddler → Two-Face.
- Villain replay mode may not end when both heroes are defeated; they rally and continue fighting.
- Three.js is imported from `https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Browser reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and WebGL performance warnings; no gameplay-breaking module error was observed.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Finish the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a complete, playable game.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside the Continue button.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing game and confirmed it includes a 3D city, campaign, combat, collectibles, riddles, character swapping, vehicles, touch controls, and replay modes.
- Added Enter/Space keyboard support to advance dialogue in `game.js`.
- Verified Enter advances dialogue through the intro and reaches the playable street-war objective.

### Active
- Test the gameplay flow and fix any blockers to completing the campaign.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test movement and combat, then progress through gang operation, clues/riddles, Riddler, Two-Face, and replay mode; fix any blockers found.
2. Save and inspect the latest screenshot following the stated viewport and JPEG constraints.
3. Review `git diff` and summarize the completed game and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, story, controls, combat, UI logic, and uncommitted dialogue keyboard change.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and touch controls.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Campaign objective chain: gang operation → eight clues → Riddler → Two-Face.
- The latest browser state is at the playable objective, “Stop the gang operation. 5 crew members remain.”
- Villain replay mode may not end when both heroes are defeated; they rally and continue fighting.
- Three.js is imported from `https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Browser reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and WebGL performance warnings; no gameplay-breaking module error was observed.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git diff` showed only the keyboard dialogue change in `game.js`.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help

## Objective
- Finish the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a complete, playable game.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside the Continue button.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.

## Work State

### Completed
- Added Enter/Space keyboard support to advance dialogue in `game.js`.
- Verified dialogue advancement reaches the playable street-war objective.
- Tested combat; attacks work, and defeating five crew members advances the campaign to the clue-search objective.

### Active
- Test campaign progression through clues/riddles, Riddler, Two-Face, and villain replay; fix any blockers.
- Save and inspect the latest screenshot following the stated viewport and JPEG constraints.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue testing clue collection and riddles, then boss fights and villain replay; fix gameplay blockers found.
2. Save and inspect a current JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.
3. Review `git diff` and summarize the completed game and reasonable assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, campaign, controls, combat, and uncommitted dialogue keyboard change.
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and touch controls.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- Campaign objectives progress from gang operation to eight clues, Riddler, then Two-Face.
- The latest browser state is at “Search Gotham for the Riddler’s evidence. Look for cyan glows.” with 0/8 clues; five crew members were defeated.
- Villain replay may not end when both heroes are defeated; they rally and continue fighting.
- Three.js is imported from `https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- Browser reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and WebGL performance warnings; no gameplay-breaking module error was observed.
- Changes are uncommitted; `git diff --check` passed, and the known diff is the dialogue keyboard change in `game.js`.

## Objective
- Finish the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a complete, playable game.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside the Continue button.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Enter/Space dialogue advancement in `game.js`.
- Added a villain-mode ending when both Batman and Robin are defeated, replacing the prior rally-and-repeat behavior.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Test campaign progression through eight key clues, riddles, both boss fights, and villain replay; fix any blockers found.
- Test the new villain-mode ending, then review the final diff and summarize the completed game and reasonable assumptions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue campaign testing from the clue-search stage; verify riddles, Riddler, and Two-Face progression.
2. Test villain replay through the new defeat ending.
3. Rerun checks, review `git diff`, and summarize the result.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign, controls, combat, and current uncommitted changes.
- `index.html`: Game UI, dialogue, and ending screens.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and responsive UI.
- `/tmp/opencode/gotham-latest.jpg`: Latest inspected gameplay screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; latest `git status --short` showed `M game.js`.
- Campaign stages are street war → eight key clues → Riddler → Two-Face; clue-search stage was active during testing.
- A collectible pickup registered a Riddler trophy as challenge 1/50, but campaign clue progress remained 0/8.
- Villain ending behavior was just changed and has not yet been browser-tested.
- Three.js loads from `https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`; a missing `/favicon.ico` and WebGL performance warnings were previously observed.

Writing18. FULLY FUNCTIONAL GADGET CONTROLS AND VEHICLES
IMPORTANT: Batman and Robin must actually be able to use their gadgets and vehicles during gameplay. Do not simply display these items on their characters or inside the Batcave. Every gadget must have a working game mechanic, animation, sound effect, and player control.
A. BATMAN'S GRAPPLE GUN
Create a fully functional fictional grapple gun for Batman.
Required features:
Batman can aim at designated grapple points.
Display a targeting indicator when a grapple point is available.
Pressing the grapple button makes Batman attach to the selected point.
Batman is pulled toward the grapple point using a smooth animation.
Batman can reach rooftops, buildings, and elevated platforms.
Allow Batman to use the grapple while exploring Gotham.
Include grapple animations, rope visuals, and sound effects.
Allow Batman to transition from grappling into gliding.
The grapple gun must work during free-roam exploration and designated missions.
B. BATMAN'S BATARANGS
Make Batman's batarangs usable as a fictional in-game gadget.
Include:
A batarang selection icon.
A throwing animation.
A visible spinning batarang.
A targeting indicator.
A return or recovery animation.
A sound effect when thrown.
A cooldown or limited-use system.
Batarangs should have gameplay interactions with designated targets, switches, and environmental objects. They can also briefly distract enemies in appropriate missions.
C. ROBIN'S GRAPPLE GUN
Robin must have his own working grapple gun.
Include:
Aiming.
Grapple-point targeting.
Pulling Robin toward rooftops.
Smooth climbing and landing animations.
Grappling between buildings.
Gliding transitions.
Robin must not simply use Batman's character model or animations. Give him his own red-and-black suit animations.
D. ROBIN WINGS
Make Robin Wings a usable fictional game gadget.
Include:
A visible equipment icon.
A throwing animation.
A spinning visual effect.
Environmental target interactions.
A recovery animation.
A cooldown system.
E. BATMAN'S SMOKE PELLETS
Allow Batman to select and activate smoke pellets.
Include:
A smoke animation.
A visible smoke cloud.
Appropriate visual effects.
A cooldown system.
An animation showing Batman moving away from the smoke.
F. VEHICLE SYSTEM – BATMOBILE
The Batmobile must be a fully modeled, drivable 3D vehicle.
Required features:
Black armored Batmobile.
Detailed exterior.
Working headlights and taillights.
Realistic wheels.
Driving animations.
Acceleration and braking.
Steering.
Reverse.
Vehicle camera.
Engine sounds.
Driving sound effects.
Collision animations.
Vehicle entry and exit animations.
Batman must be able to enter and exit the Batmobile.
Add a Batmobile summon option so the player can request the vehicle during appropriate free-roam gameplay.
The Batmobile must be usable throughout Gotham City.
G. VEHICLE SYSTEM – ROBIN'S MOTORCYCLE
Robin must have his own separate motorcycle.
Design:
Red body.
Black details.
Yellow accents.
Large R symbol.
Sport motorcycle appearance.
Realistic wheels and headlights.
Required gameplay:
Robin can approach and mount the motorcycle.
Robin can drive around Gotham.
Include acceleration, braking, steering, and reverse.
Include motorcycle engine sounds.
Add a third-person vehicle camera.
Allow Robin to dismount.
Allow the motorcycle to be summoned during free roam.
Do not replace Robin's motorcycle with the Batmobile.
H. PLAYER CONTROLS
Create a complete control system.
Automatically support the available input method.
Keyboard and mouse
WASD: Move.
Mouse: Camera.
Space: Jump.
Shift: Run.
E: Interact.
G: Grapple.
Q: Select gadget.
Left mouse button: Use selected gadget.
F: Enter or exit vehicle.
C: Switch character when available.
Controller
Create corresponding controller buttons for:
Movement.
Camera.
Jumping.
Grappling.
Gadget selection.
Gadget activation.
Vehicle entry and exit.
Character switching.
Mobile touchscreen
Because the game may be played on Android, include a proper touchscreen interface.
Display:
Left virtual joystick for movement.
Right-side camera control.
Jump button.
Grapple button.
Gadget button.
Character-switch button.
Vehicle button.
Interaction button.
Combat buttons.
Make buttons large enough to tap comfortably.
Buttons should appear contextually when appropriate.
I. GADGET AND VEHICLE INVENTORY
Create an on-screen inventory showing available equipment.
Batman:
Grapple gun.
Batarangs.
Smoke pellets.
Other available Batman equipment.
Robin:
Grapple gun.
Robin Wings.
Bo staff.
Vehicles:
Batmobile.
Robin motorcycle.
Show the selected gadget, available uses, and cooldown indicators.
J. BATCAVE VEHICLE GARAGE
Create a garage inside the Batcave.
Display:
Batmobile on its own platform.
Robin's motorcycle on a separate platform.
Vehicle lighting.
Vehicle customization area.
Vehicle selection interface.
Allow the player to walk up to each vehicle and interact with it.
K. IMPORTANT FUNCTIONALITY TEST
Before declaring the game complete, test the following:
Batman can use his grapple gun.
Batman can use batarangs.
Batman can activate smoke pellets.
Robin can use his grapple gun.
Robin can use Robin Wings.
Batman can enter and drive the Batmobile.
Robin can enter and drive his motorcycle.
Both characters can exit their vehicles.
All gadgets have working animations.
Mobile controls respond correctly.
Keyboard and controller inputs work when supported.
Character switching works during appropriate gameplay.

Required features:
Batman can aim at designated grapple points.
Display a targeting indicator when a grapple point is available.
Pressing the grapple button makes Batman attach to the selected point.
Batman is pulled toward the grapple point using a smooth animation.

Include grapple animations, rope visuals, and sound effects.
Allow Batman to transition from grappling into gliding.
The grapple gun must work during free-roam exploration and designated missions.
B. BATMAN'S BATARANGS

Include:
A batarang selection icon.
A throwing animation.
A visible spinning batarang.
A targeting indicator.
A return or recovery animation.
A sound effect when thrown.
A cooldown or limited-use system.

Aiming.
Grapple-point targeting.
Pulling Robin toward rooftops.
Smooth climbing and landing animations.
Grappling between buildings.
Gliding transitions.

Environmental target interactions.

## Objective
- Finish the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a complete, playable game.
- Implement Batman and Robin’s separate usable gadgets and vehicles for free-roam and missions.

## Requirements
- Batman and Robin must have distinct gadget systems and separate vehicles; features must be playable, not decorative.
- Include grapple aiming/targeting, rooftop traversal and glide transitions; usable batarangs/Robin Wings with cooldowns and environmental interactions; Batman smoke pellets; drivable Batmobile and Robin motorcycle.
- Support keyboard/mouse, controller when supported, and mobile touchscreen controls; show equipment and cooldown status.
- Add a Batcave garage with vehicle selection and interaction.
- Test gadget and vehicle functionality, input methods, character switching, and exit behavior before declaring completion.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside the Continue button.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- End villain mode after both Batman and Robin are defeated.
- Use simplified in-game mechanics where full simulation is impractical, without silently omitting requested functionality.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Enter and Space dialogue advancement in `game.js`.
- Added villain-mode ending when both heroes are defeated.
- Tested campaign progression through eight clues, both boss transitions, the story ending, and the villain ending.
- Verified Enter/Space dialogue advancement.
- Began replacing placeholder vehicle meshes with distinct Batmobile and Robin motorcycle models.
- Added rooftop grapple-point markers, gadget HUD/target-reticle markup, and expanded touchscreen action buttons.

### Active
- Implement the full gadget, grapple, vehicle, and input mechanics in `game.js`; the latest edits added helper functions but have not yet been connected to movement, action handlers, update loop, or rendering.
- Complete vehicle handling, summon/enter/exit controls, and vehicle camera behavior.
- Add functional controller support and improve mobile camera control.
- Implement Batcave garage interaction and vehicle selection.
- Run syntax checks and gameplay tests; capture and inspect a latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue wiring the new helpers in `game.js` into `doAction`, keyboard handlers, `move`, `interact`, and `animate`; add projectile impacts/recovery, smoke expiry, grapple rope animation, cooldown updates, and vehicle acceleration/steering/reverse.
2. Check for syntax and behavioral issues in recent edits, then implement the garage, controller support, and remaining touch controls.
3. Test the requested character/gadget/vehicle flows and run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`; inspect a screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing campaign and combat plus in-progress gadget/vehicle implementation.
- `index.html`: HUD and touchscreen controls.
- `style.css`: HUD and responsive touch-control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` previously showed `M game.js`, and subsequent edits also changed `index.html` and `style.css`.
- `game.js` has partial new helpers: `selectGrapplePoint`, `useGrapple`, `toggleGlide`, `cycleGadget`, `updateGadgetHud`, `throwGadget`, and `grappleVehicle`.
- Vehicle constructor changed to `car(x,z,type)`; batmobile and bike now use explicit `'batmobile'` and `'bike'` types.
- Building metadata now includes `h`, used to create rooftop grapple markers.
- Earlier villain-mode assumption remains: end only after both Batman and Robin are defeated.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a playable game, including usable gadgets, separate vehicles, and their use in free-roam and missions.

## Requirements
- Implement grapple targeting, rooftop traversal and glide transitions; batarangs/Robin Wings with cooldowns and environmental interactions; Batman smoke pellets; drivable Batmobile and Robin motorcycle.
- Support keyboard/mouse, controller when supported, and mobile touchscreen controls; show equipment and cooldown status.
- Add a usable Batcave garage with vehicle selection and interaction.
- Test gadget and vehicle functionality, input methods, character switching, and exit behavior before declaring completion.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside Continue.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- End villain mode after both Batman and Robin are defeated.
- Use simplified in-game mechanics where full simulation is impractical, without silently omitting requested functionality.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Enter and Space dialogue advancement and villain-mode ending after both heroes are defeated.
- Earlier campaign testing covered eight clues, both boss transitions, the story ending, villain ending, and dialogue advancement.
- Replaced placeholder vehicle meshes with distinct Batmobile and Robin motorcycle models.
- Added rooftop grapple-point markers, gadget HUD/target-reticle markup, mobile action buttons, and a central garage bay model.
- Added partial gadget helpers for grapple, glide, gadget selection/HUD, smoke pellets, thrown projectiles, and vehicle summon/enter/exit.
- Updated `interact()` to prioritize garage interaction and use planned `leaveVehicle()`, `openGarage()`, and `enterVehicle()` helpers; these helpers are not yet implemented.

### Active
- Finish wiring gadget helpers into action handlers, keyboard input, movement, and update/render loop; implement projectile impacts/recovery, smoke expiry, grapple rope animation, cooldowns, and vehicle acceleration/steering/reverse.
- Implement the referenced garage/vehicle helpers and garage selection; add controller support and mobile camera control.
- Run syntax/behavior checks and test requested gameplay flows; capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- `interact()` now references undefined `leaveVehicle()`, `openGarage()`, and `enterVehicle()`; runtime will fail when those paths are triggered until implemented.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and connect helpers in `game.js` to action handlers, keyboard input, movement, interactions, and `animate`.
2. Implement garage selection and the missing vehicle helpers, plus driving, controller input, and touch camera controls.
3. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`; test gadgets, vehicles, garage interaction, input methods, character swapping, and vehicle exits.
4. Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign, world, vehicles, garage, and in-progress mechanics.
- `index.html`: HUD and touchscreen controls.
- `style.css`: HUD and responsive touch-control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `game.js` has key bindings `F` grapple and `G` glide, while HUD hints label `G` grapple and `F` vehicle.
- Touch controls dispatch `jump`, `gadget`, and `vehicle` actions, but `doAction()` currently handles none of these.
- `grappleVehicle()` exists but is not wired; existing nearby-vehicle interaction had direct entry/exit behavior.
- Garage is centered at `(0,0,-8)`; `garageSelection` exists but selection behavior is not implemented.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a playable game, including usable gadgets, separate vehicles, and their use in free-roam and missions.

## Requirements
- Implement grapple targeting, rooftop traversal and glide transitions; batarangs/Robin Wings with cooldowns and environmental interactions; Batman smoke pellets; drivable Batmobile and Robin motorcycle.
- Support keyboard/mouse, controller when supported, and mobile touchscreen controls; show equipment and cooldown status.
- Add a usable Batcave garage with vehicle selection and interaction.
- Test gadget and vehicle functionality, input methods, character switching, and exit behavior before declaring completion.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside Continue.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- End villain mode after both Batman and Robin are defeated.
- Use simplified in-game mechanics where full simulation is impractical, without silently omitting requested functionality.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Enter and Space dialogue advancement and villain-mode ending after both heroes are defeated.
- Earlier campaign testing covered eight clues, both boss transitions, the story ending, villain ending, and dialogue advancement.
- Added distinct Batmobile and Robin motorcycle models, rooftop grapple-point markers, gadget HUD/target-reticle markup, mobile action buttons, garage bay, and garage-selection overlay.
- Implemented garage selection UI handlers and `openGarage()`, `closeGarage()`, `enterVehicle()`, and `leaveVehicle()`.
- Added basic vehicle acceleration, steering, reverse, and wheel rotation in `move()`.
- Added jump/glide physics, smoke pellet stealth timer setup, gadget cycling, and vehicle summon/ride action helper.
- Updated character swapping to exit a vehicle first and refresh gadget HUD.

### Active
- Wire `throwGadget()`, gadget cycling, jump, ride action, and mobile actions into keyboard and `doAction()`.
- Finish grapple rope/cooldown progression, projectile hit/recovery logic, smoke expiry, and gadget HUD update loop; a `stepGadgets()` insertion failed because its expected surrounding text did not match.
- Add controller input and mobile camera look.
- Verify garage UI styling, controls, syntax, gameplay flows, and latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- Gadget effects and cooldowns are not yet advanced in the animation loop; the attempted `stepGadgets()` patch failed with “Could not find oldString in game.js.”
- `doAction()` and keyboard listeners still lack the newly added gadget, jump, and vehicle actions; existing keyboard bindings still use F for grapple and G for glide.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `game.js` around `rideAction()`, `setStealth()`, `doAction()`, keyboard listeners, and `animate()`; add gadget updates using exact current context.
2. Wire keyboard and touchscreen actions, controller support, and mobile camera controls.
3. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`; test gadgets, garage/vehicles, character switching, controls, and exits.
4. Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign, world, and in-progress gadget/vehicle mechanics.
- `index.html`: HUD, garage overlay, and touchscreen controls.
- `style.css`: HUD and responsive touch-control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.
- `game.js` is densely formatted, mostly one function per line; apply edits against exact current text.
- The latest attempted patch to add `stepGadgets()` did not apply; no such helper should be assumed to exist.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a playable game, including usable gadgets, separate vehicles, and their use in free-roam and missions.

## Requirements
- Implement grapple targeting, rooftop traversal and glide transitions; batarangs/Robin Wings with cooldowns and environmental interactions; Batman smoke pellets; drivable Batmobile and Robin motorcycle.
- Support keyboard/mouse, controller when supported, and mobile touchscreen controls; show equipment and cooldown status.
- Add a usable Batcave garage with vehicle selection and interaction.
- Test gadget and vehicle functionality, input methods, character switching, and exit behavior before declaring completion.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside Continue.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- End villain mode after both Batman and Robin are defeated.
- Use simplified in-game mechanics where full simulation is impractical, without silently omitting requested functionality.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Enter and Space dialogue advancement and villain-mode ending after both heroes are defeated.
- Prior campaign testing covered eight clues, both boss transitions, the story ending, villain ending, and dialogue advancement.
- Added separate Batmobile and Robin motorcycle, rooftop grapple markers, gadget HUD/target-reticle markup, touchscreen action buttons, garage bay, and vehicle-selection overlay.
- Implemented garage selection, vehicle entry/exit, vehicle controls, jump/glide physics, smoke stealth, gadget cycling/projectiles, grapple movement, cooldowns, and gadget HUD updates.
- Wired gameplay actions to keyboard and touchscreen; added controller polling, left-stick movement, right-stick camera look, and action-button mappings.
- Fixed legacy grapple movement duplication and corrected mouse-click strike handling.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Browser opened at `http://localhost:3002`; app rendered and visible controls were confirmed in the browser snapshot. Console showed GPU performance warnings and a missing `/favicon.ico` 404, but no JavaScript errors.

### Active
- Test playable flows in browser: gadgets/cooldowns and target hits, garage and both vehicles, swapping/exiting, controller mappings, and mobile controls.
- Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot with viewport no wider than 1280px.
- Review/fix any gameplay issues found, then rerun syntax and diff checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing from the open game at `http://localhost:3002`, starting the case and exercising gameplay mechanics and controls.
2. Save and inspect the latest screenshot at viewport width ≤1280px.
3. Rerun `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`; report verified behavior and any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign, world, gadgets, vehicles, controls, and animation/update logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, garage, dialogue, and touchscreen controls.
- `style.css`: HUD and responsive touch-control styling.

- Complete the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a playable game, with usable gadgets, separate vehicles, and their use in free-roam and missions.

## Requirements
- Implement grapple targeting, rooftop traversal and glide transitions; batarangs/Robin Wings with cooldowns and environmental interactions; Batman smoke pellets; drivable Batmobile and Robin motorcycle.
- Support keyboard/mouse, controller when supported, and mobile touchscreen controls; show equipment and cooldown status.

- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- End villain mode after both Batman and Robin are defeated.
- Use simplified in-game mechanics where full simulation is impractical, without silently omitting requested functionality.

- Added Enter and Space dialogue advancement and villain-mode ending after both heroes are defeated.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a playable game, with usable gadgets, separate vehicles, and their use in free-roam and missions.

## Requirements
- Implement grapple targeting, rooftop traversal and glide transitions; batarangs/Robin Wings with cooldowns and environmental interactions; Batman smoke pellets; drivable Batmobile and Robin motorcycle.
- Support keyboard/mouse, controller when supported, and mobile touchscreen controls; show equipment and cooldown status.
- Add a usable Batcave garage with vehicle selection and interaction.
- Test gadget and vehicle functionality, input methods, character switching, and exit behavior before declaring completion.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside Continue.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- End villain mode after both Batman and Robin are defeated.
- Use simplified in-game mechanics where full simulation is impractical, without silently omitting requested functionality.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Enter and Space dialogue advancement and villain-mode ending after both heroes are defeated.
- Added separate Batmobile and Robin motorcycle, rooftop grapple markers, gadget HUD/target-reticle markup, touchscreen actions, garage bay, and vehicle-selection overlay.
- Implemented garage selection, vehicle entry/exit and controls, jump/glide physics, smoke stealth, gadget cycling/projectiles, grapple movement, cooldowns, and gadget HUD updates.
- Wired gameplay actions to keyboard, touchscreen, and controller; controller includes left-stick movement and right-stick camera look.
- Fixed legacy grapple movement duplication and mouse-click strike handling; touch camera dragging avoids triggering strikes.
- Corrected the gadget status from `Q SELECT` to `T SELECT` and separated the gadget hint lines in the HUD.
- Browser checks confirmed story dialogue advances, gadget cycling and smoke-pellet cooldown work, Robin switching and Wings throws work, and grapple reports a lock and displays its target reticle.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed before the latest HTML/CSS HUD adjustment.

### Active
- Test garage selection, driving and exiting both vehicles, controller mappings, and mobile touchscreen layout/actions.
- Verify cooldown completion, projectile target hits, and rooftop traversal/glide in browser.
- Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot with viewport width ≤1280px.
- Rerun syntax and diff checks after the latest edits.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing at `http://localhost:3002`; verify the garage, both vehicles, character switching, and exit behavior.
2. Exercise controller and touch inputs, then check mobile layout and fix any issues.
3. Save and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot at a viewport width ≤1280px; rerun `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
4. Report verified behavior and any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign, world, gadgets, vehicles, controls, and animation/update logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, garage, dialogue, and touchscreen controls.
- `style.css`: HUD and responsive touch-control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- Existing browser session is open at `http://localhost:3002`; the page was in the story campaign after dialogue advancement.
- Browser console has shown a missing `/favicon.ico` 404 and GPU-related warnings; no gameplay JavaScript errors were identified in the checks so far.
- HUD hint fix was applied after the last syntax/diff checks.

## Objective
- Complete the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a playable game, with usable gadgets, separate vehicles, and their use in free-roam and missions.

## Requirements
- Implement grapple targeting, rooftop traversal and glide transitions; batarangs/Robin Wings with cooldowns and environmental interactions; Batman smoke pellets; drivable Batmobile and Robin motorcycle.
- Support keyboard/mouse, controller when supported, and mobile touchscreen controls; show equipment and cooldown status.
- Add a usable Batcave garage with vehicle selection and interaction.
- Test gadget and vehicle functionality, input methods, character switching, and exit behavior before declaring completion.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside Continue.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- End villain mode after both Batman and Robin are defeated.
- Use simplified in-game mechanics where full simulation is impractical, without silently omitting requested functionality.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Enter/Space dialogue advancement and villain-mode ending after both heroes are defeated.
- Implemented grapple targeting, traversal, glide/jump, gadget cooldowns and projectiles, smoke stealth, HUD status, and keyboard/touch/controller action mappings.
- Added separate Batmobile and Robin motorcycle, garage vehicle selection, and vehicle driving/exit behavior.
- Browser checks confirmed story dialogue, gadget cycling, smoke cooldown, Robin switching/Wings throws, and grapple lock/target reticle.
- Browser check confirmed garage interaction, Robin motorcycle selection, driving input, and exit behavior.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed; the current uncommitted changes include `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`.

### Active
- Test Batmobile garage selection, driving, and exit; verify character switching and both characters’ vehicle restrictions.
- Test controller and mobile touchscreen layout/actions.
- Verify cooldown completion, projectile target hits, and rooftop traversal/glide in browser.
- Capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot at viewport width ≤1280px; rerun syntax and diff checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing at `http://localhost:3002`; check Batmobile use and switching between heroes and their vehicles.
2. Exercise controller and touch inputs; check mobile layout and actions.
3. Verify cooldown completion, projectile hits, and rooftop traversal/glide.
4. Save and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot with viewport width ≤1280px; rerun `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
5. Report verified behavior and any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign, world, gadgets, vehicles, controls, and animation/update logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, garage, dialogue, and touchscreen controls.
- `style.css`: HUD and responsive touch-control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- Existing browser session is open at `http://localhost:3002`; current character is Robin, on foot near the garage after driving and exiting his motorcycle.
- Browser console showed a missing `/favicon.ico` 404 and GPU-related warnings; no gameplay JavaScript errors were observed.
- Browser movement to the garage exposed nearby enemy damage during testing; Robin’s vitals decreased, but garage selection and motorcycle exit worked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a playable game, with usable gadgets, separate vehicles, and their use in free-roam and missions.

## Requirements
- Implement grapple targeting, rooftop traversal and glide transitions; batarangs/Robin Wings with cooldowns and environmental interactions; Batman smoke pellets; drivable Batmobile and Robin motorcycle.
- Support keyboard/mouse, controller when supported, and mobile touchscreen controls; show equipment and cooldown status.
- Add a usable Batcave garage with vehicle selection and interaction.
- Test gadget and vehicle functionality, input methods, character switching, and exit behavior before declaring completion.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside Continue.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- End villain mode after both Batman and Robin are defeated.
- Use simplified in-game mechanics where full simulation is impractical, without silently omitting requested functionality.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented dialogue advancement, villain-mode ending, grapple targeting/traversal, glide, gadgets/cooldowns/projectiles, smoke stealth, HUD, and keyboard/touch/controller mappings.
- Added separate Batmobile and Robin motorcycle, garage vehicle selection, driving and exit logic.
- Confirmed garage selection and exit for both vehicles; controls expose the exit prompt while riding.
- Confirmed Batmobile driving controls are wired; a simulated gamepad button triggered gadget use and a projectile hit (“BATARANG HIT · GANG LOOKOUT”).
- Confirmed grapple locks onto a point and begins pulling; mobile controls are visible at 390×844; touchscreen vehicle control exited the Robin motorcycle.
- Latest `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Captured and inspected the latest JPEG at `/tmp/opencode/latest.jpg` (viewport 390×844).

### Active
- Confirm actual vehicle motion and character-specific vehicle restriction messages; prior input tests did not conclusively demonstrate movement or restrictions.
- Verify completed grapple rooftop traversal and glide outcomes, and exercise touch movement/actions beyond control visibility and a vehicle exit.
- Physical controller testing remains unconfirmed; only a simulated gamepad API was used.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. At `http://localhost:3002`, verify driving and exiting both vehicles, and confirm each hero is restricted to their own vehicle.
2. Test touchscreen movement and actions, plus physical controller input if available.
3. Confirm grapple traversal completion and glide behavior; inspect gameplay console errors.
4. Re-run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`; if taking a visual check, save and inspect only the latest JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px.
5. Summarize confirmed behavior and any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign, world, gadgets, vehicles, controls, and animation/update logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, garage, dialogue, and touchscreen controls.
- `style.css`: HUD and responsive touch-control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- Browser console errors observed were duplicate `/favicon.ico` 404s; no gameplay JavaScript errors were reported. GPU warnings were also observed.
- Grapple initiation was confirmed, but traversal completion is still unverified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing Batman: Shadows of Gotham project as a playable game, including gadgets, traversal, vehicles, and their use in free-roam and missions.

## Requirements
- Implement grapple targeting/traversal, glide, character-specific gadgets with cooldowns and environmental interactions, and drivable Batmobile and Robin motorcycle.
- Support keyboard/mouse, controller when supported, and mobile touchscreen controls; show equipment and cooldown status.
- Add a usable Batcave garage with vehicle selection and interaction.
- Test gadget and vehicle functionality, input methods, character switching, and exit behavior before declaring completion.
- Support Enter/Space dialogue advancement alongside Continue.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots at a viewport no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.

## Decisions
- Continue the existing Three.js game and campaign rather than starting a new project.
- End villain mode after both Batman and Robin are defeated.
- Use simplified in-game mechanics where full simulation is impractical, without silently omitting requested functionality.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented dialogue advancement, villain-mode ending, grapple targeting/traversal, glide, gadgets/cooldowns/projectiles, smoke stealth, HUD, and keyboard/touch/controller mappings.
- Added separate Batmobile and Robin motorcycle, garage vehicle selection, driving and exit logic.
- Confirmed garage selection and vehicle exit for both rides; HUD exposes the exit prompt while riding.
- Simulated gamepad gadget input produced a projectile hit (“BATARANG HIT · GANG LOOKOUT”).
- Confirmed grapple lock/pull initiation and touchscreen controls at 390×844; a touchscreen vehicle action exited the Robin motorcycle.
- Latest `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/latest.jpg` at 390×844.

### Active
- Confirm actual vehicle motion and verify that each hero is restricted to their own vehicle; recent tests showed the ride/exit state but did not conclusively demonstrate movement or switching restrictions.
- Verify completed grapple rooftop traversal, glide outcomes, and touchscreen movement/actions.
- Physical controller testing remains unconfirmed; only simulated gamepad API input was used.
- Recheck gameplay console errors after tests.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. At `http://localhost:3002`, test driving and exiting both vehicles and verify each hero’s vehicle restriction; ensure character switching occurs when a vehicle is occupied.
2. Test touchscreen movement/actions, glide and completed grapple traversal; test a physical controller if available.
3. Check gameplay console errors, then rerun `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
4. If taking another visual check, save and inspect only the latest JPEG at a viewport no wider than 1280px.
5. Summarize confirmed behavior and remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign, world, gadgets, vehicles, controls, and animation/update logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, garage, dialogue, and touchscreen controls.
- `style.css`: HUD and responsive touch-control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes in `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- Browser console errors observed were duplicate `/favicon.ico` 404s; no gameplay JavaScript errors were reported. GPU warnings were also observed.
- Grapple initiation is confirmed, but rooftop traversal completion is not.
- `swap()` calls `leaveVehicle()` before changing the player, but the latest attempted touch-button `.click()` while riding did not switch heroes; retest using actual supported input.

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser

  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element

  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions

  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)
